Flagship process case study

From working draft
to a 48-page report.

This is an independent production study for the fictional Calloway Holdings. The company and financial data are synthetic. The reconstructed Word file below was created from the same content model to demonstrate the kind of unstructured source material a publication designer has to turn into a dependable document system.

48 mapped pages12 columns27 financial reconciliationsINDD + IDML handoff
01 / SOURCE

Start with content, not a pretty spread.

The reconstructed Word draft deliberately mixes rough hierarchy, notes to the designer, tables, image placeholders and inconsistent direct formatting. It is not claimed as a historical client file; it is a transparent demonstration of the source-to-layout problem.

Download the reconstructed Word source ↓
02 / CONTENT AUDIT

Turn the draft into a page architecture.

The content was mapped before layout: letters, strategy, operating divisions, people and sustainability, governance, statements and notes each need different reading behaviours but one report system.

01Overview & performance

Headline measures, contents and the reading route.

02Leadership narrative

Chair and CEO letters with sustained reading pages.

03Strategy & divisions

Three operating businesses with charts, diagrams and decision points.

04People & sustainability

Measures with explicit denominators and methodology.

05Governance

Roles, review cycle and remuneration reference tables.

06Financial reference

Statements plus five notes that reconcile back to the group model.

03 / DESIGN SYSTEM

Approve the rules before scaling the pages.

The report uses an A4, 12-column structure with 18 mm margins, 5 mm gutters and a baseline rhythm. The anatomy proof below is an actual InDesign export with the grid overlaid—not a recreation made for the website.

A412 columns18 mm margins5 mm guttersbaseline rhythmserif + sans hierarchy
04 / REPRESENTATIVE APPROVAL

Test different content types before building all 48 pages.

A useful approval set should test the system, not three variations of the cover. These pages cover a performance page, a division section and a dense financial statement.

05 / FULL DOCUMENT

The real test is whether the system survives page 48.

The complete report moves through narrative, charts, tables, diagrams, governance and financial notes. The overview below is assembled from the actual exported pages.

Read the complete PDF ↗Inspect all 48 pages ↓
06 / QA & HANDOFF

Delivery is part of the design job.

The native package contains the editable document, IDML fallback, linked assets, fonts and screen/print outputs. Automated checks recorded 27 financial reconciliations, eight bookmarks and 18 link destinations. The print PDF remains provisional until a physical proof and printer profile are approved.

Finished publication / selected pages

The system after it scales to 48 pages

Project intention

A substantial corporate report connecting headline performance to the chapters behind it. The design needs consistency without flattening the differences between financial information, narrative, and supporting detail.

Design decisions

A restrained report architecture keeps long-form prose, sections, and data legible as readers move through the document.
